name: Long-term archival storage of ice cores at -36 C with sampling in a -24 C examination room (NSF Ice Core Facility)
plain_name: Keep ice cores frozen in a national archive freezer
description: Ice cores from Antarctica and Greenland are curated as 1 m sections in tubes on shelves inside a walk-in archive freezer held at -36 C so that trapped gases, chemistry and stratigraphy are preserved; cores are cut and sampled for researchers in an examination room held at -24 C.
keywords: Keep ice cores frozen in a national archive freezer

sources.citation: About - U.S. National Science Foundation Ice Core Facility (NSF-ICF, formerly National Ice Core Laboratory)
NSF Ice Core Facility - Services (storage of cores and use of the facility)

requirements.rationale: Archive storage set point -36 C (237.15 K); the storage space must hold this temperature.
Core examination and sub-sampling are done at -24 C (249.15 K) in a separate room; optional for a storage-only machine.
Cores are stored as 1 m sections in tubes, so the storage space must accept a 1000 mm long item along its loading/shelf axis (either key satisfies).
